title: Last-call windows, opt-in migration tooling, and signal-driven deprecation process for old model versions
creator: Asha Nair
description: Scope: Define and implement a customer-centric deprecation lifecycle for legacy model versions that combines: 1) a configurable 'last-call' opt-in window per customer where they can request extended support; 2) an automated migration assistant that surface recommended pin targets, compatibility shims, and code snippets; and 3) telemetry-driven triggers (quality regressions, usage drop, compatibility signals) to drive notices and automated escalation. Goals: minimize customer surprise, reduce helpdesk lift during sunsets, preserve latency/cost SLAs by migrating users off old heavy variants, and create observable signal chains so we can measure migration success and regressions. Out of scope: permanent removal of on-prem private deployments (handled by Private team runbook).
acceptance_criteria: Template notice sequences (early-warning, last-call, final-sunset) are authored and stored in Confluence and can be published from Console to selected customers
Opt-in window mechanism in Console allows customers to request a 30/60/90-day extended support with SLA implications and is recorded in audit logs
Migration assistant (CLI + Console flow) suggests target model variants, quantization recommendations, and automated pin changes with a dry-run preview
Telemetry triggers publish to a dashboard: 1) migration progress % by customer, 2) pinned vs unpinned distribution, 3) quality regression alerts linked to prompt set tests
Runbook for support and sales is published and includes escalation paths, refund/migration compensation guidance, and rollback steps
updates: 2025-09-12: Scoped initial proposal with Eng and Design. Agreed to include opt-in windows and automated pin suggestions as MVP features.

2025-09-15: ENG spike for compatibility shim approaches completed. Two viable patterns identified: server-side adapter and client-side polyfill. Engineering prefers server-side adapter for faster rollout.
2025-09-18: Design reviewed two Console flows (inline banner vs. dedicated Migration panel). PM/Design decided on a dedicated panel to reduce cognitive load and support complex opt-in flows.
2025-09-20: Draft notification templates reviewed by Legal and Support. Legal requested an explicit SLA change clause for opt-in extensions.
2025-09-24: Telemetry prototype pushed to staging. Dashboard wireframe validated; need to add per-customer migration success metric (binary success/failed) and time-to-migrate median.
2025-09-25: Blocker identified: audit-log retention for opt-in events requires storage config from Infra (ENG-19780). Raised dependency; mitigation planned for next sprint.
comments: Luca Martinez (Eng): Server-side shim will add ~5% tail-latency in worst-case; recommend gating by customer tier and providing opt-out. Need perf test matrix before rollout.
Priya Shah (Design): Migration panel should include 'preview impact' showing token cost delta and qualitative sample outputs comparing source->target models.
Jonas Becker (Support): Add templated troubleshooting steps for hallucination regression post-migration and a default rollback play that Support can trigger for enterprise customers.
Mei Wong (Legal): Confirmed language for opt-in SLA extension and data retention; requested marketing review of customer-facing notice tone.

Asha Nair (PM): We'll run a pilot with 3 customers (one AI-native startup, one mid-market, one enterprise) to validate tooling and comms before broad roll-out. Pilot targets to be onboarded by 2025-10-01.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive automated pinning reduces support burden but may break integrations; chosen approach is suggestion + one-click pin with dry-run and rollback.
Metric choices: track 'migration success' as backed-by-production-traffic for two weeks post-migration and 'quality delta' using standard prompt set.
Fallback policy: if compatibility shim causes >2% error-rate increase for a pinned customer, automatically revert to previous model and notify stakeholders.
